summary: This article explains how lifting weights with good form gradually builds muscle strength, and why correct technique and rest matter more than lifting heavy too soon.
introduce: Show the title “Weightlifting: Building Strength Safely” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a careful, skillful way of doing something
damage or harm done to the body
the way a person holds or positions their body

challengeTerms.def: the study of how the body moves and is positioned during physical activity
the growth or thickening of muscle fibers from training
a gradual increase in demand placed on the body to cause it to adapt

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that learning correct form matters more than lifting heavy weights? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Use the words technique and patience to explain how weightlifting builds strength safely.
struggling: Pre-teach technique, injury, and posture with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use biomechanics, hypertrophy, and overload in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
